answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a slashing stake: every new identity must lock real value at a shared ledger vertex, and peers verify a signed receipt before granting it a quill to transact. A fake army is no longer free, since each forged agent needs its own bond, so the attacker pays roughly linearly per identity. If one is caught double-spending, its stake is burned, turning a pearl of collateral into a permanent loss. Honest agents reclaim their bond plus small fees, making impersonation far costlier than cooperation.
